items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: I'm not talking about the folklore, now, I'm not talking about the Blind Lemon Jeffersons and the Boogie-Woogie or Booga-Rooga on the guitar.

ctx.x: Yes, yeah, we talked about that.

Same thing. So many of the things with which we are confronted in life are not real. They are real, but we don't see them as being real. Can you imagine me thinking 'til I was thirty that "walking Jerusalem." I thought I had to be in heaven. I thought when he said, "Go to Jerusalem" he meant that, oh boy, you know what I mean, I'm going to die and the casket'll be pink and, you know, and I'll... and all that business. And then Bethlehem. I thought Bethlehem was in heaven. And then don't worry, Dan, millions of…

You have some guys that come up to try to tell you how great a musician is, or he can't play, you know what I mean. "I just don't like him," "He can play the piano /but I just don't like him." This is what they say about me: I talk too much. But I talk because it's my prerogative. I can talk if I want to. I came through the period of jazz from the late teens until today and I like to think that I can have something
